title: Seattle, the second room
logline: A second Seattle apartment, smaller, boxes by the door again — this time from a divorce, not a move. Drawn from the one line she wrote: 'a smaller place, near the water.' Water in the window.

panels.composition: A small apartment with boxes by the door, a mattress on the floor, one lamp, and a window with the Sound in it. A green coat on the only chair. Nothing on the walls except a rectangle where a frame was.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a small bare apartment with moving boxes by the door and a mattress on the floor, one lamp, a window showing distant water, a green coat over the only chair, a pale rectangle on the wall where a picture hung, no people, no words
image.notes: The divorce (Julian to 2021). Reserved beyond 'a smaller place, near the water.'

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The second room. A rectangle where a frame was.
